question: Can a cross-validation-tuned LightGBM model on richer early-adoption features predict final cascade popularity better than a neural network on basic early-spread features, when both are tested on the same held-out simulated cascades?
method: Independent-cascade simulation on a Barabasi-Albert graph (networkx); label = log final size; single 80/20 split (seed 42); MLP baseline vs CV-tuned LightGBM; 3 seeds each.

dataset.name: Simulated independent-cascade cascades on a Barabasi-Albert graph (networkx)

metric_name: R2 on log(final cascade size) on held-out test set
baseline: scikit-learn MLPRegressor (64-32 hidden, standardized inputs) on early-spread features: cumulative adopter counts over the first 4 time steps. Stand-in for the paper's neural encoder.
improved: LightGBM regressor tuned by 3-fold CV grid search on the training set, using the same early counts plus early-adopter degree statistics, growth rates and time-to-k-adopters.
notes: Simulated data, not the paper's Twitter/Digg cascades; the paper's transformer+GCN model is not reproduced (MLP stand-in). Single graph and single split. Baseline uses fixed hyper-parameters, not tuned. Best LightGBM CV params: {'learning_rate': 0.03, 'min_child_samples': 10, 'n_estimators': 200, 'num_leaves': 15}. Spearman and MAE are secondary and not used for selection.
